attribution_limitations: Platelet and MCV values differ between the text and Table 1: the text gives platelets 18 and MCV 122 as initial values, whereas the table gives platelets 30 and MCV 102 on Day 1 and 18 and 122 on Day 2.
The text says platelets rose to 223 within 10 days, but Table 1 gives 144 on Day 10 and 223 on Day 12.
The text reports Hb 101 g/dL after IV iron whereas Table 1 gives 101 on Day 30 in g/L; the Table 2 title refers to day 19, which is not a Table 1 column.
Table 1 bilirubin of 186 on Day 25 follows 34 on Day 10, and Day 25 neutrophils 0.3 sit beside white cell count 3.2; values are retained as printed.
The author states oral maintenance therapy followed parenteral repletion "as per guidelines" without naming the agent, dose or time.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Blood smear shows a tear drop cell (arrow) typical of megloblastic anaemia

Figure 2
Peripheral blood film showing macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophil (arrow), typical of megaloblastic anaemia.

Figure 3
Bone marrow trephine (low power) shows evidence of dyserythropoiesis and myeloid maturation arrest, with megakaryocytes of variable maturity, consistent with megaloblastic changes.

Figure 4
Bone marrow trephine (high power) showing megaloblasts with nuclear cytoplasmic asynchrony (arrows), consistent with megaloblastic change due to vitamin B12 and folate deficiency.

limitations: Figures 1-4 were inspected in the separate visual submission; this annotation keeps caption-level visual status.
Table 1 dash cells are recorded as not done per the table legend; no zero values were substituted.
Folate 1.1 at the GP visit has no stated unit.
Platelet, MCV and Day 10 platelet text values conflict with Table 1 and are kept review-only without reconciliation.
Hb 101 g/dL (text) versus g/L (Table 1) and the Table 2 reference to day 19 are not corrected.

claims.text: A 65-year-old woman presented after six months of progressive tiredness, loss of appetite and weight loss with new-onset mild confusion. History included multiple sclerosis, hypertension, osteoarthritis and hiatus hernia; she lived alone, did not smoke, abstained from alcohol and had a chronically poor appetite. A GP visit three months before admission had led to folic acid 5 mg daily for two months.
